stories.title: Govt to chair EU meeting on Ceuta migrant crisis
stories.summary: An emergency meeting of EU interior and justice ministers to discuss the migrant crisis in Ceuta will take place later today. It will be convened by Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan as Ireland holds the EU Presidency. The images of over 50,000 people swimming across the border from Morocco to the Spanish North African territory of Ceuta pushed immigration right to the top of the list of issues to be dealt with during Ireland's EU Presidency. Spain has blamed disinformation on social media for the surge of mostly young men across the border, and said 48,000 of them were quickly returned to Morocco.

stories.title: Donald Trump set to travel to Doonbeg for Irish Open
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is set to travel to Ireland next month for a visit that will include his attendance at the Irish Open at his golf course in Doonbeg, Co Clare, and events in Dublin. This date is to ensure he will be in the US for the annual commemoration of the 11 September terrorist attacks, and that he will be in Doonbeg in time for the end of the Irish Open on 13 September. Mr Trump's visit will also include a trip to Dublin, which is likely to involve a meeting with Taoiseach Micheál Martin. However, sources said it is highly unlikely that Mr Trump will give a speech to the Dáil or Seanad, or attend any events at Leinster House, as TDs and senators are not due to return from their summer break until 16 September.

stories.title: Manufacturing growth drives pick-up in hiring, PMI shows
stories.summary: The manufacturing sector expanded strongly in July as output and new orders grew at robust rates and companies hired at the fastest pace since May 2022, a business survey showed today. The AIB Ireland Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), compiled by S&P Global, rose to 55.1 in July from 54.9 in June. "Output rose strongly in July, albeit the pace of increase eased slightly from June, with respondents citing continued healthy order books," David McNamara, AIB's chief economist, said. Companies linked higher output to robust order books and improving demand conditions. Total new business expanded for a 19th consecutive month.

stories.title: EU chief urges 'united action' after Ceuta incident
stories.summary: EU chief Ursula von der Leyen has called for "united action" on border security after a migrant rush on Spain's North African territory of Ceuta triggered a public spat between Madrid and several European partners. It comes after officials said the death toll from the mass rush reached at least 72 after five more bodies were found along the North African coast. More than 50,000 people crossed into Ceuta by land and sea in an unprecedented surge that began on Thursday at one of the European Union's only two land borders with Africa, prompting alarm across the bloc. "From this incident, it is clear that we must do more to further strengthen our borders at critical points," Ms von der Leyen wrote in a letter to Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.

stories.summary: Shamrock Rovers will look to keep alive their hopes of European group stage football as they take on KF Egnatia in the Europa League third round qualifying at Tallaght Stadium on Tuesday. The Hoops dropped down to the Europa League after a disappointing second-half performance at home saw them lose to Armenian side Ararat-Armenia in the Champions League qualifiers. Trailing 2-0 from the first leg in Armenian, Rovers produced a wonderful first 45 minutes in the second leg to level the tie up as 2-2 by half-time, but they were unable to build on that and a 73rd-minute goal by Brazilian striker Sandro Lima saw them drop down a tier. A win for Rovers would move them into the Europa League play-off round for a match against Lillestrom of Norway, a prize that also guarantees participation in the group stages of the Conference League.

stories.title: Waterford beat Shels to massively boost survival hopes
stories.summary: Waterford FC boosted their SSE Airtricity Men's Premier Division survival hopes with a huge 1-0 victory over Shelbourne at the RSC, as Tommy Lonergan's second-half strike secured three priceless points for Graham Coughlan's side. While Waterford city and county enjoyed the festivities of the August Bank Holiday weekend, with Spraoi and the All Together Now festival drawing large crowds, there was plenty for the home supporters to celebrate at the RSC as the Blues delivered one of their biggest results of the season. Backed by a crowd of 1,977, Waterford moved three points clear of bottom side Sligo Rovers thanks to a committed and disciplined performance that was crowned by Lonergan's 48th-minute diving header. The hosts were the brighter side throughout much of the contest and could have been ahead inside six minutes. Padraig Amond picked out Jordan Houston, whose cross found Lonergan, but the striker's looping header struck the near post with Shelbourne goalkeeper Ed Beach beaten.

stories.title: RTÉ Supporting the Arts this August
stories.summary: From major festivals and theatrical premieres to exhibitions, concerts and family-friendly celebrations, audiences nationwide are invited to experience the richness and diversity of Ireland's cultural landscape throughout the month. National Heritage Week returns with hundreds of events taking place across Ireland, encouraging people of all ages to explore and celebrate the country’s rich natural, built and cultural heritage. Through guided tours, exhibitions, talks, workshops and community initiatives, Heritage Week continues to foster a deeper appreciation of Ireland’s shared history and traditions. August brings a number of exciting productions to the Abbey Theatre. Highlights include Ulster American, starring Matthew Broderick, running on the Abbey Stage from 12 to 22 August 2026, a sharp satirical comedy exploring identity, privilege and power. Later in the month, Mirandolina, Marina Carr's adaptation of Carlo Goldoni's La Locandiera, opens on 28 August, marking its Irish premiere as part of an international co-production. Kilkenny Arts Festival returns this August with an ambitious multidisciplinary programme featuring music, theatre, literature, visual arts and performance. Widely regarded as one of Ireland’s premier arts festivals, it attracts leading Irish and international artists while transforming the city into a vibrant cultural hub.

stories.title: Thousands flee wildfires in US city of Spokane
stories.summary: Fast-moving fires left a trail of destruction in the northwestern US city of Spokane, with officials reporting hundreds of structures reduced to cinders. Thousands of people were ordered to evacuate their homes Saturday and overnight into Sunday, as three separate fires broke out in and around the city in the east of Washington state. The National Weather Service (NWS) had warned of "extremely critical fire weather conditions" in the area due to strong winds and exceptional dryness. Video of the aftermath on Sunday showed scores of homes burned to the ground, with only their brick fireplaces and foundations remaining, while other houses nearby escaped practically unscathed.

stories.title: Ospreys or Scarlets face axe as WRU outlines cut plans
stories.summary: Wales are to go ahead with plans to cut their number of professional franchises from four to three, spelling the end for either the Ospreys or Scarlets, both former winners of the United Rugby Championship. The Welsh Rugby Union on Wednesday confirmed the proposed change to the professional game and plans to establish three men's teams from the 2028/29 season – one based in the capital, one in west Wales and one in east Wales. Cardiff, owned by the Welsh Rugby Union, and Dragons, an independently backed business, are set to be given licences, leaving Swansea-based Ospreys and Llanelli-based Scarlets to compete for the remaining spot. Ospreys have won the URC, in its previous guise, four times, most recently in 2012.

stories.title: inside The Centre Culturel Irlandais: where Ireland & Europe meet
stories.summary: As Ireland assumes the Presidency of the Council of the European Union, the Centre Culturel Irlandais in Paris presents an ambitious autumn and winter programme of exhibitions, debates, theatre and music. The CCI's Rosetta Beaugendre reflects on the Centre's ongoing role as a cultural bridge between Ireland and Europe. Modern Ireland owes much to the European Union, born itself in the aftermath of conflict and out of a desire to avoid history being repeated. The country's attachment since 1973 to seeking common ground found concrete expression nearly 25 years ago when the Centre Culturel Irlandais was inaugurated in one of the world's finest cultural capitals, in the heart of Europe, in the former Irish College. This elegant 18th century building had after all concentrated the learning, the hopes and maturing of generations of young Irishmen on the Continent. In 2002, although not yet 30, I felt the resonance of this confident even audacious affirmation of Ireland’s place in the European story. Now, in 2026, as the country takes over the presidency of the Council of the EU, we are on the threshold of a season of ambitious events and collaborations led by our inspired director, Nora Hickey M'Sichili. The CCI could be considered the undiplomatic diplomats of the party, teasing out the kind of issues that Fintan O’Toole has dubbed in the past 'unknown knowns’. For instance, our rentrée exhibition looks at Ireland’s housing crisis and, as such, provides a conduit for Irish citizens’ concerns that have filtered through the percolator of artists’ psyches and practices to be expressed in material form. Everyone Should Have a Home explores frustrations, contradictions, grey areas but equally includes proposals for innovative 21st century housing. In addition, we have teamed up with Marsh’s Library to present a timely exhibition Gulliver 300, in our Old Library, that highlights the continuing relevance of Swift’s critique of human nature, societal norms and flaws… one need only think of the satirist’s 'Modest Proposal’ in response to overcrowding in Dublin’s 18th century tenements!

stories.title: Anne Hathaway celebrates 25 years of The Princess Diaries

In a post on Instagram accompanied by a video of her making the film, Hathaway said: "25 years later and it's still one of the most magical things that has ever happened to me. stories.title: Met Gala 2027 will honour controversial designer John Galliano
stories.summary: The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced that its next exhibition will celebrate the career of John Galliano, whose renowned stint as the Creative Director at Dior ended after he was filmed making antisemitic and racist remarks outside a Paris cafe in 2011. John Galliano: Horizons will be on display at The Met from May 9, 2027 until January 9, 2028, and will be a career-spanning look at a figure largely regarded by the fashion industry as one of the most influential designers of the last number of decades. The exhibition will be kicked off by the annual Met Gala on 3 May, where the A-list attendees will be sure to pay homage to Galliano's work. With this exhibit, Galliano becomes only the third living designer to have their work featured in a solo exhibition by the institute, after Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo of Comme des Garçons in 2017.

stories.title: 25 US states sue to block Trump tariffs
stories.summary: Twenty-five US states, nearly all led by Democrats, sued US President Donald Trump's administration yesterday over wide-ranging tariffs, arguing that the president had exceeded his authority in imposing the new levies on dozens of countries. The states filed suit at the US Court of International Trade in New York, asking that judges halt the implementation of the tariffs, declare them unlawful and order the US government to issue refunds. The legal challenge relates to Mr Trump's latest tariffs of 10% to 12.5% imposed against 60 trading partners, which formed the bulk of US imports last month. The tariffs were imposed after probes by the US Trade Representative's (USTR) office over allegations of "forced labour," conducted under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

stories.title: Finn Harps members to vote on proposed takeover
stories.summary: One of the last remaining fan-owned clubs in the League of Ireland, Finn Harps, will soon decide on a multi-million euro takeover from former Philippines manager and businessman Alfredo "Freddy" Razon Gonzalez. Harps who are based in Ballybofey, Co Donegal have been part of the Irish football for more than 70 years and currently sit bottom of the SSE Airtricity Men's First Division. The club’s co-operative society has 2,179 members; however, the club’s board has said voluntary effort alone is not a sustainable foundation in the modern game. "The very survival of the club is at risk. It’s up to the people to decide. We can't force it on anyone, but the feedback that we've had so far has been extremely positive," he said.

stories.title: Labour's Bev Craig elected mayor of Greater Manchester
stories.summary: The UK's ruling Labour Party comfortably retained the mayoralty of Greater Manchester following an election triggered by new Prime Minister Andy Burnham's return to parliament. Bev Craig, the leader of Manchester City Council, was elected after winning 47.15% of the votes in the first round. The anti-immigration Reform UK party, which had been riding high in national polls, came in second place with a 21% share. Without the 50% of votes needed to win outright, the counting proceeded to a second round.

stories.title: BP's Q2 profit more than doubles from a year ago
stories.summary: BP's second-quarter profit more than doubled to $5.73 billion on higher oil and gas prices and strong refining margins, it reported today, as CEO Meg O'Neill outlined the energy group's priorities. Oil majors have benefited this year from market volatility caused by the US-Iran conflict, which has disrupted energy flows and tightened global supplies. BP's second-quarter underlying replacement cost profit, its version of net income, beat expectations of $5.11 billion in a company-provided poll of analysts and rose from $2.35 billion a year earlier. It said it would increase its dividend by 4% to 8.66 cents per ordinary share for the second quarter.

stories.title: Ajax can take inspiration from Shelbourne as they rebuild
stories.summary: When Shelbourne step onto the pitch at the Johan Cruyff Arena for the first time, John Russell and his players will warm up underneath banners representing different moments in Ajax's history. There's banners dedicated to their 36 league titles, others to their European Cup successes and some to show their victories in the Intercontinental Cup. The unifying theme is how they were achieved, with the club’s guiding philosophy. It’s based around the manipulation of space, pressing high, and passing the ball while giving youth a chance. Rinus Michels was the pioneer, Stefan Kovács took it to the next level and Louis van Gaal brought it into the modern age. Johan Cruyff was its greatest disciple, with the midfielder using it to win Barcelona their first European Cup in 1992.
